title: The authored creatures deform on the GPU and finally deform in the game at all; a #swarm lab studies look and cost together
context: Measurement had shown rendering and simulation are both affordable, so the owner asked for the shader port as a FEATURE rather than an optimisation, plus a lab studying enemies for look-and-feel and telemetry. Tracing the code first found that the amoeba, phage and jellyfish have no TICKS entry: in gameplay they were static clouds, because waveJelly only ever ran in the unit viewer's one-at-a-time carousel. The claimed 17x speed win therefore did not exist in gameplay, and was corrected before any work started.
outcome: src/content/dot-wobble.js owns the motion constants and GENERATES the GLSL; creatures.waveJelly and swimWave read the same constants, so the two implementations cannot drift (the GLSL half cannot run in Node, so a constant changed on one side would silently make the lab and the game show different creatures). src/fx/dot-material.js is a drop-in replacement for PointsMaterial: td-tab writes material.opacity for emerge and death fades and material.color.setHex for the slow field every frame and is at its line budget, so `color` is the live uniform value and `opacity` is a defined setter; nothing in td-tab changed. units.js: the three authored creatures now wobble in the vertex shader, and scoutufo and shellback moved their swim off the CPU, which removes the last per-frame re-pose in gameplay. Behaviour is pinned by goldens captured before the extraction: both functions are unchanged to nine decimals. Two bugs surfaced only in a browser probe, neither reachable from Node: makeCloud seeded its buffer with waveJelly(base, 0), which is not the identity because the ripple term is spatial, so the shader deformed an already-deformed body; and the TICKS fallback overwrote the wobblers' tick slot, which would have frozen the wobble at t=0 with no error anywhere. New lab src/labs/swarm-tab.js at labs.html#swarm: body, form (dot cloud or jelly), count to 3000, density, spread, layout and turntable on the left, and a readout giving cost in ms, microseconds per body, percent of a 60 fps frame, draw calls, points and triangles. It measures with a tight loop and gl.finish rather than rAF deltas, because rAF measures vsync — a first cut of the earlier benchmark reported a flat 16.6 ms for every variant at every count for exactly that reason. Measured in the lab: 1000 amoebas at 474,020 points cost 1.2 ms, 1000 phages 1.4 ms, 300 jelly bodies at 1.52M triangles 0.3 ms.
alternatives: Add a crowd mode to units-tab.js: rejected, that module documents its own one-unit-at-a-time rationale and is already 1401 lines; a crowd study is a different question and belongs in a sibling.
Give every roster body the wobble: rejected, the rest read as machinery and keep their transform idles; only the three authored organic bodies and the two swimmers deform.
Write the GLSL by hand next to the JS: rejected, two copies of 0.18 with no failing test between them is the drift this design exists to prevent.
evidence: test/dot-wobble.mjs: eight tests including waveJelly and swimWave goldens captured before the extraction, and an assertion that every content constant appears in the generated shader.

scripts/browser-test.mjs case swarm-study: asserts the shader compiles and draws, that the authored creatures report motion 'wobble', that swimmers report 'swim' and roster bodies 'static', and that a jelly draws triangles and no points.
npm test, npm run check, npm run build, npm run test:browser and node scripts/browser-test.mjs --dist all pass.
Lab readout on an M4: 1000 amoebas 1.2 ms at 474,020 points; 300 jelly bodies 0.3 ms at 1.52M triangles.
